root_scope: Rational Hodge Conjecture for smooth projective complex varieties: every rational (p,p) class is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes.
object_context: Let f:X->S be a smooth projective family of complex varieties, s0 in S, and alpha a flat rational Hodge class already algebraic on X_s0 by a fixed finite signed rational witness z0. Fix one algebraic irreducible local Hodge-locus branch T through s0. This atom isolates only the effectivity/algebraization step after a compatible all-Artin-order tower of exact witness components has been constructed over the completed local ring A=O^_T,s0.
quantity_of_interest: Whether compatible formal closed-subscheme witness towers over Spec(A/m^n) algebraize over Spec(A), and exactly which residuals remain before pointwise variational algebraicity on an actual branch neighborhood.
structural_coordinates: A is a Noetherian complete local ring obtained from an algebraic finite-type Hodge-branch model; algebraicity of the Hodge locus is source-bound to Cattani-Deligne-Kaplan.
X_A := X x_T Spec(A) is separated and of finite type (indeed projective in the application).
The central rational witness is represented after denominator clearing as z0=(1/N) sum_i n_i [Z_i,1] with fixed finite integer coefficient vector.
For every indexed component i, an all-order candidate is a compatible cartesian tower Z_i,n -> X_n over A/m^n; compatibility, not merely existence at each order, is mandatory.
Grothendieck existence/effectivity over the completion is distinct from descent from Spec(A) to a henselian/etale/Zariski neighborhood in T.
Formal effectivity is distinct from cohomology-class identity, flatness in the exact Hilbert/Chow category, branch domination, monodromy, degeneration, and root initial algebraicity.
equivalent_formulations: FORMAL_EFFECTIVITY question: from compatible Z_i,n closed in X_n with Z_i,1 proper, obtain Z_i closed in X_A reducing to Z_i,n for all n.
SIGNED_WITNESS effectivity: perform the previous construction componentwise while retaining N and the integer coefficient vector (n_i).
RESIDUAL_SPLIT: after formal effectivity, separately test exact-category flatness/class preservation and descent from the completed local base to an actual branch neighborhood.
solved_analogues: Grothendieck existence/algebraization for compatible closed subschemes over a complete Noetherian base (Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.28.1 / tag 0898).

Grothendieck existence for finitely presented flat modules with proper support (Stacks Project, More on Flatness, Theorem 38.28.9 / tag 0CTK), retained only as a boundary/source for flatness rather than silently identifying modules with closed-subscheme witnesses.
near_solved_analogues: Artin approximation/algebraization can approximate or descend formal objects under additional hypotheses; no exact neighborhood-descent theorem is imported into this atom.
H4d1d shadow route in PR #119: proper witness-incidence domination of a reduced Hodge branch; retrieved as proposal/shadow routing evidence only.

method_transfers.source_context: Grothendieck existence for closed subschemes over a complete Noetherian ring
method_transfers.method: Treat an all-order compatible witness tower as a formal closed subscheme and apply the exact effectivity theorem componentwise.
disanalogies: the theorem yields effectivity over the completion, not automatic descent to an open Hodge-branch neighborhood
it does not certify the Gauss-Manin class equals alpha
it does not by itself certify exact Hilbert/Chow flatness after algebraization
it assumes the all-order tower that the deformation problem must still construct
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the remaining Hodge deformation route focus on constructing a compatible exact-category tower and a separate completion-to-neighborhood descent certificate, rather than carrying an undifferentiated algebraization residual?

explicit_disanalogies: The root Hodge conjecture asks initial algebraicity; this atom assumes a central algebraic witness.
Independent lifts at each Artin order do not constitute a compatible inverse system and cannot trigger the theorem.
An algebraized closed subscheme over Spec(A) is not yet a family over a Zariski or etale neighborhood containing nearby complex fibres of T.
A componentwise effectivity theorem does not solve component switching or monodromy when the chosen signed decomposition is not preserved.
Reduced-branch pointwise algebraicity and full nonreduced scheme-theoretic lifting are different targets.
analogy_scan_notes: Nonmathematical formal-to-concrete analogies were rejected because they do not preserve completion, proper support, closed-subscheme effectivity, rational coefficients, or Hodge-local-system interfaces.
